source_refs.quote: On or about September 10, 1959 the respondent landlord let out the premises in suit to the appellant

law_refs.quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952

tests.objects: Respondent landlord; appellant tenant; asserted subletting of shop to Sohan Singh during tenancy commencing in 1959.
tests.opposition: The appellant denied that any subletting occurred. No exact subletting date is given; the post-1952 conclusion concerns only the temporal setting of an alleged act by this tenant.
tests.rationale: Any subletting by the appellant of a tenancy first created in September 1959 would necessarily postdate 9 June 1952, and the claim was filed in September 1962. This supports the date condition of the alleged disposition, not that any disposition occurred.

source_refs.quote: The Rent Controller was of the view that the appellant was the legally Wedded wife of Sohan Singh.
Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.
That finding was confirmed in appeal by the Rent Control Tribunal, Delhi.
Neither any talks regarding sub-letting took place in my presence, nor the rent was paid in my presence,

law_refs.quote: In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; Sohan Singh alleged subtenant and husband; Royal Dispensing Chemists and Druggists; entire shop.
tests.opposition: The landlord alleged a subtenancy and an exceptionally large rent paid by Sohan Singh. A typed document also recorded recognition of the appellant as his wife, and no direct witnessed rent payment was identified in the supplied testimony.

opposition_refs.quote: she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh
It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh.
The true copy disclosed that the appellant was accepted as the wife of Sohan Singh.

tests.rationale: The Rent Controller's no-subletting conclusion, affirmed on appeal, refutes the asserted tenancy relationship at those prior stages. The contrary landlord allegations do not independently show rent paid, transfer of estate interest and a right to possession against the tenant.

source_refs.quote: she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh
from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.

law_refs.quote: In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; Sohan Singh; shop; no separately described assignment.
tests.opposition: The pleaded theory was subletting to the husband, not a distinct assignment; his running a shop does not itself prove or disprove a transfer of all tenancy rights.
tests.rationale: Nothing in the allowed record identifies an assignment arrangement to which the all-rights-divestment test can reliably be applied. The refusal to rate this unused alternative is not a finding of no assignment.

source_refs.quote: was running a business under the name of Royal Dispensing Chemists and Druggists in the shop.
from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.

law_refs.quote: "parting with possession" must have been by the tenant.

tests.objects: Appellant tenant; Sohan Singh as person operating chemist shop; physical shop use versus legal right to possess it.
tests.opposition: The landlord alleged Sohan Singh was a subtenant. The appellant characterized him as her husband and herself as an occasional participant; the prior finding rejected subletting but did not expressly adjudicate a separate divestment of legal possession.

opposition_refs.quote: she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh
Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.

tests.gap_reason: No document or prior finding settles whether the appellant divested both physical possession and the legal right to possess the shop in favour of Sohan Singh. Operation of his business does not alone resolve those rights.
tests.rationale: Sohan Singh's business use could coexist with the appellant's tenancy rights. The prior no-subletting finding bears against exclusive transfer, yet does not resolve the distinct parting-with-possession requirements; C04 remains unresolved.

source_refs.quote: she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh

law_refs.quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord;

tests.objects: Respondent landlord; appellant tenant; alleged disposition of whole shop to Sohan Singh.
tests.opposition: The landlord's allegation and the appellant's denial concern whether a disposition took place, not whether written consent had been given for it.
tests.gap_reason: There is no stated written-consent instrument, denial of consent, or finding addressing whether consent in writing was obtained for the alleged Sohan Singh arrangement.
tests.rationale: Silence about written permission cannot support the required proposition that written consent was not obtained, irrespective of the prior rejection of subletting.

source_refs.quote: from the time of the lease the business of a Chemist was being run there in the premises by her husband and she also occasionally helped him in the running of the business.
Sohan Singh and the appellant were living together as husband and wife and, therefore, there was no question of any sub--letting by the appellant of the premises.
The true copy disclosed that the appellant was accepted as the wife of Sohan Singh.

law_refs.quote: If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession

tests.objects: Appellant tenant and alleged husband Sohan Singh; shop and claimed shared family/business use.
tests.opposition: The landlord alleged a separate shop subtenancy and substantial rent. A common marital household and occasional help are material to concurrent use, but do not themselves establish retained legal possession of this shop.

opposition_refs.quote: It was further alleged that the appellant was charging a fabulous amount as rent from her sub-tenant Sohan Singh.

tests.gap_reason: The record does not state whether the appellant continued to hold an enforceable right to concurrent use and legal possession of the shop, or whether an agreement wholly ousted her; business participation alone is not conclusive.
tests.rationale: Prior findings and the appellant's account support a retained-user explanation and weigh against total exclusion. But C06 asks specifically about legal possession of the relevant shop, for which the required right or ouster fact is not expressly resolved.

source_refs.quote: The premises consisted of a shop.
she had sub-let the entire premises to one Sohan Singh

law_refs.quote: the whole or any part of the premises

tests.objects: Entire shop demised to appellant; entire shop was the object of respondent's asserted transfer to Sohan Singh.
tests.opposition: The appellant denied subletting itself, not the identification of the shop as the premises alleged to have been transferred.
tests.rationale: The alleged transaction expressly covers the whole demised shop, a statutorily included scope. C07 does not establish that a transfer actually took place.
